clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A nurse is preparing to move a portable compressed-oxygen cylinder within the hospital. Which transport method is consistent with OSHA guidance?

options.A: Attach the cylinder firmly to a suitable transport device so it cannot fall or strike other objects.
options.B: Roll the cylinder horizontally along the floor while keeping one hand on the valve assembly.
options.C: Carry the cylinder by the valve protection area because the destination is nearby.
options.D: Place the unsecured cylinder on a stretcher and stabilize it by surrounding it with linens.

semantic_correction.rationale: OSHA's healthcare eTool directs facilities to secure compressed-gas cylinders and not to drop, roll, or drag them. OSHA's interpretation of 29 CFR 1910.101(b) further explains that a suitable hand truck, cylinder pallet system, or similar material-handling device may be used with the cylinder properly attached so it cannot fall or strike another object. Therefore, option A is the supported transport method. Rolling, carrying by the valve area, or placing the cylinder unsecured on a stretcher does not meet that guidance.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Transport compressed-gas cylinders on a suitable device with the cylinder firmly secured against falling or striking objects, and avoid rolling or dragging cylinders.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely longest. OSHA directly supports firm attachment to a suitable transport device and avoidance of rolling/dragging; the revised item tests that transport decision without introducing context-dependent valve-cap or cylinder-use assumptions.

option_audit.A: Correct. OSHA permits suitable material-handling devices when the cylinder is properly attached and protected from falling or striking objects.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. OSHA healthcare guidance states not to roll compressed-gas cylinders horizontally.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Valve or valve-protection components are not an appropriate carrying method for a cylinder.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Soft padding does not constitute firm securing of the cylinder to a suitable transport device.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone provides the OSHA-supported secured transport method.
cueing_check: All four options are transport methods of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or uniquely long correct answer identifies A.
